answer: Reputation clawback per operator. Each identity is a vertex in a shared graph, and when one is caught faking, the system invalidates every identity that operator controls, not just the offending one. That forces an attacker to build a whole crystal of mutually consistent histories for every fake persona, since a single detection shatters the set. An atlas mapping operators to their clusters is recomputed weekly, so the per-identity cost includes the full reconstruction labor for all linked accounts.
